BURHAN:v4p406/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p406/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p406/r5.claim: The third type is ما that blocks its governing particle from acting, occurring between a governor and its governed noun or phrase.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r4.claim: Most readers pronounce الدواب with a doubled b; al-Zuhrī lightens it to avoid adjacent silent consonants, compared with a hamzated reading of الضالين.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: والدواب، مشدد الباء والزهري: بتخفيفها، كراهية التضعيف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r5.claim: مختلفة modifies an omitted خلق; كذلك completes the comparison with the fruits and mountains, and the pause after كذلك is appropriate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r5.anchor: ومختلفة، صفة لمحذوف، أي خلق مختلف ألوانه كذلك، أي كاختلاف الثمرات والجبال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r6.claim: The true scholars fear God because they know His attributes, oneness, and what is possible, necessary, or impossible for Him; greater knowledge brings greater fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r6.anchor: والعلماء هم الذين علموه بصفاته وتوحيده وما يجوز عليه وما يجب له وما يستحيل عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya's alternative attachment of the previous phrase: إنما separates it syntactically from what follows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r7.anchor: وهذا الاحتمال لا يصح، لأن ما بعد إنما لا يمكن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r8.claim: A report says the verse was revealed about Abū Bakr, whose fear of God became visibly apparent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p30/r8.anchor: في أبي بكر الصديق، وقد ظهرت عليه الخشية حتى عرفت فيه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reports al-Zamakhsharī's restrictive view that only scholars fear God; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says exclusivity depends on context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r1.anchor: ومن ادعى أن إنما للحصر قال: المعنى ما يخشى الله إلا العلماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r2.claim: Most readers put Allah in the accusative and العلماء in the nominative; a reading attributed to ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Abū Ḥanīfa reverses them, interpreted as reverential awe, though Abū Ḥayyān doubts its attribution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r2.anchor: وروي عن عمر بن عبد العزيز وأبي حنيفة عكس ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r3.claim: The sentence follows the signs in ألم تر and reads as saying that the Messenger and people like him, who know God, are the ones who fear Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r3.anchor: وجاءت هذه الجملة بعد قوله: ألم تر، إذ ظاهره خطاب للرسول، حيث عدد آياته وأعلام قدرته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r4.claim: God's might explains fear through His punishment of sinners, while His forgiveness invites the repentance of the obedient.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p31/r4.anchor: إن الله عزيز غفور: تعليل للخشية، إذ العزة تدل على عقوبة العصاة وقهرهم

ASAD-NOTES:35:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:intro/r3.claim: The surah centers on God's power to create and resurrect and His revelation through prophets; knowledge leads to awe of the Almighty and the forgiving God.
ASAD-NOTES:35:intro/r3.anchor: Almost the whole of Al-Fatir deals with God's unique power to create and to resurrect

STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah’s main focus is God’s oneness as the sole Creator and Sustainer, contrasting divine Power with claims made for idols.
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r6.anchor: The main focus of the sūrah is upon the Oneness of God as the only Creator and Sustainer of existence

TABATABAI:35:37-38/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r5.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r5.claim: Al-Majma reports al-Sadiq's definition of scholars as those whose actions match their words; someone whose deeds contradict their speech is not a scholar, and the most knowledgeable of God are most fearful of Him.
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r5.anchor: روي عن الصادق عليه السلام أنه قال يعني بالعلماء من صدق قوله فعله

TABATABAI:35:37-38/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r6.speaker: أبو حمزة عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r6.claim: A report in Rawdat al-Kafi from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, conveys the same point about true knowledge and fear of God.
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r6.anchor: وفي روضة الكافي بإسناده عن أبي حمزة عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام ما في معناه

TABATABAI:35:37-38/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r7.speaker: الحسن عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r7.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Hakim distinguishes useful knowledge in the heart from knowledge on the tongue, which is God's proof against people.
TABATABAI:35:37-38/r7.anchor: عن الحسن قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r9.claim: The passage answers opponents who demand to see the threatened punishment before they will believe in the Qur'an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r9.anchor: not willing to believe in the Qur’ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r3.claim: The following passage answers opponents' objections and demands, then points to the inevitable fate of those denying truth through doubts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r3.anchor: The succeeding verses deal with the objections

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r1.claim: The verse laments people demanding the promised doom to reject the Qur'an's monotheism and warnings, and says they do so to harass the Prophet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r1.anchor: This verse expresses sorrow at people who in order to reject the message of monotheism of the Qur’ān and its warnings about the punishments of the Herein and the Hereafter would demand that they be shown the promised doom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r2.claim: The Prophet brings glad tidings of mercy to believers who do good and warns rejecters of God's wrath; his duty ends with delivering the message, while God decides whether and when to punish.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r2.anchor: The Prophet’s responsibility ends after he delivers these glad tidings and warnings.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r3.claim: The statement that most people do not know expresses sorrow: a messenger gives people a chance to gain mercy, yet they demand punishment instead.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r3.anchor: such is the misfortune of people that they demand punishment instead of mercy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r4.claim: A messenger's warning conclusively communicates truth; rejection then brings destruction under God's established practice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p299/r4.anchor: when the Almighty sends His messenger to a people, then the truth is conclusively communicated to them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p300/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p300/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p300/r1.claim: Earlier messengers warned their own peoples, whereas Muhammad, the final messenger, was sent to all humanity; Qur'anic styles and earlier-scripture prophecies attest this.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p300/r1.anchor: since Muh@ammad (sws) is the last of the prophets and messengers, he was sent towards all mankind.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p300/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p300/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p300/r2.claim: These words remind the People of the Book, who were supporting Quraysh, that Muhammad's message also determines their fate and they should consider the consequences.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p300/r2.anchor: the messenger they are opposing in such a vehement manner is not merely a deliverer of glad tidings and warnings to the Quraysh; he will also decide the fate of the People of the Book.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r4.claim: The conflict between belief and disbelief, like the creation of light and darkness, serves divine wisdom; only people with knowledge and cognizance value these blessings and accept faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r4.anchor: this clash between belief and disbelief is also based on God’s wisdom

ALUSI-FULL:v30p206#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p206#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p206#2/r6.claim: The link to fear also recalls that only the learned among God’s servants fear Him; al-Junayd says satisfaction corresponds to strength of knowledge and rootedness in recognition.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p206#2/r6.anchor: وإنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء ولذا قال الجنيد قدس سره الرضا على قدر قوة العلم

DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.claim: He says the seeker of knowledge and seeker of worldly wealth are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge increases God's approval, while wealth-seeking deepens transgression; he cites two verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: منهومان لا يشبعان: صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا ولا يستويان

SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r1.claim: مختلف is an adjective of an omitted subject, with the preceding prepositional phrase as predicate: a kind among people varies in color; an anonymous poetic example shows active participle government.
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r1.anchor: مختلف نعت لمنعوت محذوف هو مبتدأ، والجار قبله خبره، أي: من الناس صنف أو نوع مختلف؛ وكذلك عمل اسم الفاعل كقول الشاعر:

SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r2.speaker: ابن السميفع
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfi' reads ألوانها with feminine suffix.
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع " ألوانها " وهو ظاهر.

SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r3.speaker: الزهري
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r3.claim: Al-Zuhri lightens باء in والدواب to avoid meeting two sukuns, as in الضالين and جأن.
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r3.anchor: وقرأ الزهري " والدواب " خفيفة الباء فرارا من التقاء الساكنين، كما حرك أولهما في " الضألين " و " جأن ".

SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r4.claim: Most plausibly كذلك connects backward, describing variation like that among fruits and mountains; stop there. Ibn Atiyya connects it forward, but إنما blocks that operation and al-Dani calls the stop complete.
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r4.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه متعلق بما قبله أي: مختلف اختلافا مثل الاختلاف في الثمرات والجدد. والوقف على " كذلك ".

SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya attaches كذلك to what follows, comparing creation and varied colors with scholars' fear; the author rejects the syntax.
SAMIN-DURR:35:28/r5.anchor: والثاني: أنه متعلق بما بعده، والمعنى: مثل ذلك/ المطر والاعتبار في مخلوقات الله تعالى واختلاف ألوانها يخشى الله العلماء. وإلى هذا نحا ابن عطية وهو فاسد

SAMIN-DURR:35:28#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:28#2/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:35:28#2/r1.claim: The common reading puts Allah in the accusative and العلماء in the nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:35:28#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { إنما يخشى الله } العامة على نصب الجلالة ورفع " العلماء " وهي واضحة.

SAMIN-DURR:35:28#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:28#2/r2.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز وأبو حنيفة وأبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:35:28#2/r2.claim: They reverse the case endings, interpreted as meaning only scholars among God's servants truly revere Him, like the variant at 2:124.
SAMIN-DURR:35:28#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن عبد العزيز وأبو حنيفة فيما نقل الزمخشري وأبو حيوة - فيما نقل الهذلي في كامله - بالعكس، وتؤولت على معنى التعظيم

ASAD-NOTES:35:27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:27/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:27/r1.claim: Asad's translation glosses those endowed with knowledge as having innate knowledge and standing in awe of God.
ASAD-NOTES:35:27/r1.anchor: only such as are endowed with [innate] knowledge

ASAD-NOTES:35:27#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:27#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:27#n19/r1.claim: Asad connects the beauty of nature's varied colors with 16:13 as evidence of God's creative power.
ASAD-NOTES:35:27#n19/r1.anchor: where the splendour of nature ("the beauty of many hues") is spoken of as an evidence of God's creative power.

ASAD-NOTES:35:27#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:27#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:27#n20/r1.claim: True knowledge is spiritual realization that observable phenomena are not all reality and that a realm lies beyond created perception; Asad links this to 2:3, note 3.
ASAD-NOTES:35:27#n20/r1.anchor: spiritual knowledge, born of the realization that the phenomena which can be observed do not comprise the whole of reality

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r1.claim: Khashya is fear mixed with reverence, usually arising from knowledge of what is feared; scholars know God best and therefore most revere Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r1.anchor: الخشية خوف يشوبه تعظيم ولذلك أكثر ما يكون ذلك إذا كان الخاشي يعلم ماذا يخشى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r2.speaker: قسم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r2.claim: Some say khashya means the most intense form of fear.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r3.claim: He illustrates fear as anticipating harm: Aal Imran's command to fear enemies occurs amid the expected danger of battle.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1091/r3.anchor: آية آل عمران في سياق توقع مكروه، في سياق القتال

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p346/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p346/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p346/r1.claim: Against the passage's background, the righteous realize and refine their capacities while the truth is conclusively delivered to wrongdoers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p346/r1.anchor: potentials of the righteous materialize and are polished and the truth is conclusively delivered to the wrong-doers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r1.claim: Verses 23–26 are a parenthesis addressing the Prophet; after it, the discourse returns to its original theme, including the effects of rain and Qur'anic guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r1.anchor: Verses 23-26 are parenthetical in nature and address the Prophet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r2.claim: Rain produces varied growth; likewise the Qur'an develops the righteous while exposing evil in others, as Satan instigates his followers to oppose it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r2.anchor: Through it the abilities and potentials of the righteous develop while the evil found in others is exposed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r3.claim: Alwān can mean types or sorts as well as colours, and it carries that broader sense in the verse's next portion too.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350/r3.anchor: it also means “types” and “sorts”. In the next portion of this verse also, the word is used in this very meaning.

IBNHIBBAN:461/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:461/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:461/r1.claim: Usama b. Zayd relates the Prophet's tears for a dying child and teaching that mercy is placed in human hearts; the repeated “only ... from His servants” construction echoes 35:28.
IBNHIBBAN:461/r1.anchor: فقال له سعد بن عبادة ما هذا يا رسول الله قال رحمة جعلها الله في قلوب عباده

IBNHIBBAN:3158/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:3158/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:3158/r1.claim: Usama b. Zayd reports the Prophet's tears at Zaynab's dying daughter and his explanation that tender weeping is mercy from God, with mercy shown to merciful people.
IBNHIBBAN:3158/r1.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إنما هي رحمة جعلها الله في قلوب عباده وإنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحماء"

IBNHIBBAN:3158/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:3158/r2.speaker: author
IBNHIBBAN:3158/r2.claim: Ibn Hibban's chapter treats the report as evidence that one may weep at a child's death unless grief becomes discontent.
IBNHIBBAN:3158/r2.anchor: إنما هي رحمة جعلها الله في قلوب عباده وإنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحماء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r7.claim: Some identify those who fear as scholars, citing 35:28; since knowledge can invite vanity and pride, the reminder of God’s greatness protects scholars from these faults.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r7.anchor: من يخشى هم العلماء لقوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r1.claim: The phrase means “some of the people, beasts, and livestock,” or “some among them are varied in color,” like 2:8; it coordinates with the preceding sentence and follows its syntax.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r1.anchor: أي ومنهم بعض مختلف ألوانه أو بعضهم مختلف ألوانه على ما ذكروا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r2.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r2.claim: Irshād says nominal clauses describe ongoing color variation, unlike the preceding verbal clause for fruits emerging; only fruit variation is tied to a prompting question about seeing.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r2.anchor: أن إيراد الجملتين أسميتين مع مشاركتهما لما قبلهما من الجملة الفعلية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r3.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r3.claim: Al-Baḥr says the question about seeing seeks agreement about something especially obvious; al-Ālūsī notes this conflicts with Irshād’s claim that fruit variation is less obvious.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r3.anchor: بخلاف أحوال الجبال والناس وغيرهما فإنها مشاهدة غنية عن التأمل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r4.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r4.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads الدواب with a light bāʾ to avoid two vowelless consonants, as some readers hamza ولا الضالين for the same reason.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r5.speaker: ابن السميقع
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ reads ألوانها with feminine agreement.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r6.claim: كذلك is an accusative adjective for the verbal noun of مختلف: variation of the same kind as with fruits and mountains; it completes the preceding clause, and reciters agree that stopping here is good.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r6.anchor: في محل نصب صفة لمصدر مختلف المؤكد والتقدير مختلف إختلافا كائنا كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r7.claim: The scholars’ fear completes 35:18 by naming those among people who fear God, after indicating the honor of fear, the ugliness of its opposite, warning the heedless, and recalling divine power.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r7.anchor: إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, the clause follows the distinction between people’s inner ranks by analogy and their outward ranks by direct description, giving each kind of difference its fitting explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r8.anchor: أو بعد بيان إختلاف طبقات الناس وتباين مراتبهم أما في الأوصاف المعنوية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r9.claim: Another parsing makes كذلك the predicate of an omitted subject: the matter is as described; the next clause shifts indirectly to God’s friends and indicates that knowledge brings fitting fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r9.anchor: وقيل ( كذلك ) في موضع رفع خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r10.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r10.claim: Ṣāḥib al-Kashf says the nominative, omitted-subject parsing is clearer because it creates a decisive transition in the discourse.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p190#2/r10.anchor: قال صاحب الكشف : والرفع أظهر ليكون من فصل الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attaches كذلك to the following clause as its cause: reflecting on God’s creations and their varied colors leads scholars to fear Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r1.anchor: وقال إبن عطية يحتمل أن يكون ( كذلك ) متعلقا بما بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r2.speaker: السمين
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r2.claim: Al-Samīn rejects that attachment because إنما cannot govern backward and because reciters stop at كذلك.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r2.anchor: ورده السمين بأن إنما لا يعمل ما بعدها فيما قبلها وبأن الوقف على كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r3.claim: Al-Khafājī approves al-Samīn’s objection but says it does not weaken the omitted-subject reading, since that reading does not make إنما govern backward and the stopping rule does not settle it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r3.anchor: وأرتضاه الخفاجي وقال : وبه ظهر ضعف ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj, transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir, says that just as livestock differ in color, people differ in their fear of God.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r4.anchor: أخرج إبن المنذر عن إبن جريج أنه قال في الآية كما أختلفت هذه الأنعام

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls Ibn Jurayj’s comparison weak; he considers the majority reading most apparent and the omitted-subject transition more precise and subtle.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r5.anchor: وهذا عندى ضعيف والأظهر ما عليه الجمهور وما قيل أدق وألطف

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r6.claim: The scholars here know God, His fitting attributes, actions, and affairs, not merely grammar or morphology; the more one knows God, the more one fears Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r6.anchor: والمراد بالعلماء العالمون بالله عزوجل وبما يليق به من صفاته الجليلة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r7.speaker: عطاء عن موسى
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r7.claim: Al-Dārimī transmits from ʿAṭāʾ that Moses asked who was wisest, richest, and most God-fearing; God said the most fearful is the one who knows Him best.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r7.anchor: روى الدارمي عن عطاء قال : قال موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r8.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r8.claim: A sound Prophetic report says, I am the most God-fearing and most pious of you.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r8.anchor: وصح عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أنا أخشاكم لله وأتقاكم له

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in reports cited by Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Ṭabarī, glosses the scholars as those who know God has power over everything.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r9.anchor: فسر إبن عباس كما أخرج عنه إبن المنذر وإبن جرير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r10.claim: Fronting God as object identifies the people who fear Him—the scholars; later order would emphasize God as the only one feared, as in 9:18, which is not the present point.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r10.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لأن المقصود بيان الخاشين والأخبار بأنهم العلماء خاصة دون غيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r11.claim: This wording implicitly rebukes obstinate unbelievers as ignorant of God and His attributes, explaining why they neither fear Him nor dread His punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191/r11.anchor: بل يقتضي الأول ليكون تعريضا بالمنذرين المصرين على الكفر والعناد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r1.claim: Some deny that إنما restricts the claim to scholars, but al-Ālūsī dismisses this denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r1.anchor: وأنكر بعضهم إفادة ( إنما ) هنا للحصر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r2.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز وأبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r2.claim: A reading attributed to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Abū Ḥanīfa puts God in the nominative and scholars in the accusative; Ibn al-Jazarī attacks it, and Abū Ḥayyān doubts its authenticity.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r2.anchor: وروى عن عمر بن عبدالعزيز وأبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنهما قرءا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī mentions the anomalous reading; Abū al-Qāsim Yūsuf ibn ʿAlī ibn Junāda also records it from Abū Ḥaywa in al-Kāmil.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r3.anchor: وإنما ذكرها الزمخشري وذكرها عن أبي حيوة أبو القاسم يوسف بن علي بن جنادة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r4.claim: One view takes fear metaphorically as reverence, since what is revered inspires awe; another takes it as choosing, as in the poem about selecting one’s cousins.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r4.anchor: وخرجت على أن الخشية مجاز عن التعظيم بعلاقة اللزوم فإن المعظم يكون مهيبا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r5.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r5.claim: The poem’s phrase خشيت بني عمي uses خشيت in the sense of choosing or selecting.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r5.anchor: وقيل الخشية ترد بمعنى الإختيار كقوله خشيت بني عمي فلم أر مثلهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r6.claim: God’s might obliges fear because it signals power to punish; forgiveness and mercy are attributed only to one capable of punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r6.anchor: تعليل لوجوب الخشية لأن العزة دالة على كمال القدرة على الإنتقام

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r7.claim: Another view treats غفور as rhetorical completion (takmīl), paralleling a verse by al-Ghanawī cited earlier.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r7.anchor: من باب التكميل نظير ما في بيت الغنوي المذكور آنفا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r8.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r8.claim: Some transmitted reports say the verse was revealed concerning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, whose fear of God became visibly apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p191#2/r8.anchor: والآية على ما في بعض الآثار نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r3.claim: The masculine pronoun is used because the phrase begins with min.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r3.anchor: لأجل "من" وقيل: رد الكناية إلى ما في الإضمار، مجازه:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r4.claim: Another analysis returns the pronoun to an implicit phrase meaning there are things of varied colors among these creatures.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r4.anchor: وقيل: رد الكناية إلى ما في الإضمار، مجازه: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام ما هو مختلف ألوانه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r5.claim: Thus means colors vary as among fruits and mountains; the preceding statement ends here and the next begins anew.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r5.anchor: يعني كما اختلف ألوان الثمار والجبال، وتم الكلام هاهنا ثم ابتدأ فقال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says those who know God's might, majesty, and authority are the ones who fear Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد إنما يخافني من خلقي من علم جبروتي وعزتي وسلطاني.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r7.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r7.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that some people shunned a dispensation the Prophet had allowed; he said he knew God best and feared Him most.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r7.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها: صنع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا فرخص فيه، فتنزه عنه قوم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r8.claim: The Prophet said that if people knew what he knew, they would laugh little and weep much.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r8.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لو تعلمون ما أعلم لضحكتم قليلا ولبكيتم كثيرا".

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r9.speaker: مسروق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r9.claim: Masrūq says fear of God is sufficient knowledge, and feeling safe from God is ignorance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r9.anchor: وقال مسروق: كفى بخشية الله علما وكفى بالاغترار بالله جهلا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r10.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r10.claim: Al-Shaʿbī told a man that the true scholar is one who fears God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p419/r10.anchor: فقال الشعبي: إنما العالم من خشي الله عز وجل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p420/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p420/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p420/r1.claim: God is mighty in His kingdom and forgiving toward His servants' sins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p420/r1.anchor: عزيز في ملكه غفور لذنوب عباده.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r1.claim: People, animals, and livestock vary in color just as fruits and mountains do.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r2.claim: Only scholars truly fear God: fear requires knowledge of the one feared and His attributes and acts, so greater knowledge brings greater fear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r2.anchor: إذ شرط الخشية معرفة المخشي والعلم بصفاته وأفعاله

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r3.claim: The Prophet says he is the most God-fearing and mindful of God among them, illustrating the link between knowledge and fear.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r4.claim: Bayḍāwī follows the statement about fear with God’s acts as evidence of His complete power.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r4.anchor: ولذلك أتبعه بذكر أفعاله الدالة على كمال قدرته،

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r5.claim: Putting God before the scholars as subject restricts who fears; reversing order reverses emphasis.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r5.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لأن المقصود حصر الفاعلية

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r6.claim: A variant reads God in the nominative and “scholars” in the accusative, taking fear metaphorically as reverence that inspires awe.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r6.anchor: وقرىء برفع اسم الله ونصب العلماء على أن الخشية مستعارة

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r7.claim: God’s might and forgiveness explain fear: He punishes persisting tyrants and forgives the repentant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:28-29/r7.anchor: تعليل لوجوب الخشية لدلالته على أنه معاقب للمصر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r7.claim: Al-dawābb originally includes anything that creeps on earth, then commonly refers to riding animals; livestock is added to explicitly include all kinds.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r7.anchor: في الأصل لما دب على الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r8.claim: The colors of the people, creatures, and livestock differ like the fruits and mountain paths; one underlying earth has homogeneous substances but varying qualities, against natural causation.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r9.claim: The variety in creation proves God acts by choice and can make one thing light for some and blindness for others; this leads to asking who truly fears Him and excludes the possibility of an ignorant saint.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p221/r9.anchor: ثبت بهذا البرهان أنه سبحانه فاعل الاختيار

BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r1.claim: In the well-known reading, God is the object and the scholars are the subject: only scholars fear God, because fear requires knowledge.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r2.speaker: السهرودي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r2.claim: Al-Suhrawardi says that anyone who does not fear God lacks knowledge; the scholar is a jurist who acts on what he knows.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r2.anchor: قال السهرودي في الباب الثالث من عوارفه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r3.claim: For the alternate reading, the author invokes reciprocal reverence: scholars honor God, and God honors them for their knowledge.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r4.speaker: محمد بن القاياتي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r4.claim: Asked how to understand the alternate reading, al-Qayati answered with a poetic example of revering a beloved who has no power over the speaker.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r4.anchor: محمد بن القاياتي عن توجيه هذه القراءة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r5.claim: God is mighty and over all affairs; the contrasts in creation show that nothing He wills is difficult, and His might inspires fear.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r6.claim: The description as forgiving encourages those who turn their hearts to God, since He can erase their sins.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p222/r6.anchor: في أنه يمحو ذنوب من يريد منهم فيقبل

DURR-FULL:v7p18/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p18/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p18/r7.claim: As mountain colors vary, so do the colors of people, beasts, and livestock.
DURR-FULL:v7p18/r7.anchor: اختلفت ألوان هذه الجبال وألوان الناس والدواب والأنعام كذلك

DURR-FULL:v7p18/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p18/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p18/r8.claim: It was said that awe of God is sufficient knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v7p18/r8.anchor: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} قال: كان يقال كفى بالرهبة علما

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says fruits include red, white, green, and black; people include red, black, and white; beasts and livestock likewise vary in color.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {مختلفا ألوانها} قال: منها الأحمر والأبيض والأخضر والأسود وكذلك ألوان الناس

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r3.claim: Abū Mālik compares the differing colors of people, beasts, and livestock to the varied colors of mountains, then cites the scholars' fear of God.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r3.anchor: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام} قال: كذلك اختلاف الناس والدواب والأنعام كاختلاف الجبال

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r4.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r4.claim: Abū Mālik adds that there is no merit in what precedes the statement that only scholars fear God.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r4.anchor: ثم قال {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} فلا فضل لما قبلها

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the mountain bands vary, just as people's, animals', and livestock's colors vary; people likewise differ in their fear of God.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {ومن الجبال جدد بيض} قال: طرائق مختلفة كذلك اختلاف ما ذكر

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr associates the passage's themes with fear, faith, obedience, and diversity of colors.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال: الخشية والايمان والطاعة والتشتت في الألوان

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines the scholars as those who know God and fear Him.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} قال: العلماء بالله الذين يخافونه

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the scholars are those who know that God has power over everything.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} قال: الذين يعلمون أن الله على كل شيء قدير

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd distinguishes knowledge from abundant narration: knowledge is fear of God.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: ليس العلم من كثرة الحديث ولكن العلم من الخشية

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r10.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r10.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr defines a scholar as one who fears God.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r10.anchor: عن يحيى بن أبي كثير قال: العالم من خشي الله

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r11.speaker: صالح أبو الخليل
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r11.claim: The person most knowledgeable of God is the one most fearful of Him.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r11.anchor: عن صالح أبي الخليل رضي الله عنه في قوله {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} قال: أعلمهم بالله أشدهم له خشية

DURR-FULL:v7p19/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r12.speaker: رجل
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r12.claim: A saying transmitted through Abū Ḥayyān al-Taymī divides scholars into those who know God and His commands, those who know only God, and those who know only His commands.
DURR-FULL:v7p19/r12.anchor: عن أبي حيان التيمي عن رجل قال: كان يقال العلماء ثلاثة

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r1.speaker: رجل
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r1.claim: The three classes are defined: one fears God and knows legal limits and duties; one fears Him but does not know them; one knows them but does not fear Him.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r1.anchor: فالعالم بالله وبأمر الله: الذي يخشى الله ويعلم الحدود والفرائض

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r2.speaker: مالك بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r2.claim: Mālik ibn Anas says knowledge is not abundant narration but a light God casts into the heart.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r2.anchor: عن مالك بن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: إن العلم ليس بكثرة الرواية إنما العلم نور يقذفه الله في القلب

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan defines faith as fearing God unseen, desiring what He desires, and avoiding what displeases Him; he then recites the verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r3.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: الإيمان من خشي الله بالغيب ورغب فيما رغب الله فيه

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r4.speaker: مسروق
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r4.claim: Masrūq says fear of God is sufficient knowledge, while admiring one's deeds is sufficient ignorance.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r4.anchor: عن مسروق قال: كفى بالمرء علما أن يخشى الله وكفى بالمرء جهلا أن يعجب بعمله

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd likewise says fear of God is enough knowledge and self-delusion is enough ignorance.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: كفى بخشية الله علما وكفى باغترار المرء جهلا

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r6.claim: Mujāhid defines a jurist as one who fears God.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه قال: الفقيه من يخاف الله

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r7.speaker: داود
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r7.claim: A saying attributed to David praises God's exaltedness and says those nearest to Him fear Him most; one without fear lacks knowledge, and wisdom without obedience is no wisdom.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r7.anchor: عن العباس العمي قال: بلغني أن داود عليه السلام قال: سبحانك تعاليت فوق عرشك

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd repeats that knowledge is fear of God, not a large number of narrations.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: ليس العلم بكثرة الرواية ولكن العلم الخشية

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r9.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r9.claim: The Prophet divides knowledge into knowledge in the heart, which benefits, and knowledge on the tongue, which is God's proof against creation.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r9.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: العلم علمان علم في القلب فذاك العلم النافع

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r10.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r10.claim: Ḥudhayfa says it is enough knowledge for a person to fear God.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r10.anchor: عن حذيفة قال: بحسب المرء من العلم أن يخشى الله

DURR-FULL:v7p20/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a Qur'an bearer should be recognized by night worship, daytime fasting, grief, tears, silence, and humility, and should avoid loudness and harshness.
DURR-FULL:v7p20/r11.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: ينبغي لحامل القرآن أن يعرف بليله إذا الناس نائمون

DURR-FULL:v7p21/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r1.claim: Wahb reports Ibn ʿAbbās telling disputants that God's servants silenced by awe are eloquent scholars; when God's majesty overwhelms them, their hearts break and tongues fail, then they hasten to righteous deeds.
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r1.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه قال: أقبلت مع عكرمة أقود ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بعدما ذهب بصره

DURR-FULL:v7p21/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r2.claim: Among the maxims attributed to ʿUmar: answer one who wrongs you by obeying God; presume the best of a brother and construe a Muslim's words favorably; accept suspicion if you expose yourself to it.
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r2.anchor: قال: وضع عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه للناس ثماني عشرة كلمة

DURR-FULL:v7p21/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r3.claim: ʿUmar advises keeping one's secrets, staying with truthful friends, speaking truth even at personal cost, and avoiding irrelevant matters, needless questions, and requests to ill-wishers.
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r3.anchor: قال: وضع عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه للناس ثماني عشرة كلمة

DURR-FULL:v7p21/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r4.claim: ʿUmar warns against false oaths and wicked company, urges caution even with friends except the God-fearing, humility at graves and in obedience, resistance to sin, and consultation with those who fear God.
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r4.anchor: قال: وضع عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه للناس ثماني عشرة كلمة

DURR-FULL:v7p21/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r5.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r5.claim: Asked about the scholar and worshipper, the Prophet says the scholar's excellence over the worshipper is like his own excellence over the least among the people.
DURR-FULL:v7p21/r5.anchor: عن مكحول قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن العالم والعابد فقال: فضل العالم على العابد

DURR-FULL:v7p22/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p22/r1.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p22/r1.claim: The Prophet says God, angels, heavenly and earthly beings, and even fish in the sea pray for teachers of good.
DURR-FULL:v7p22/r1.anchor: ثم تلا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} ثم قال إن الله وملائكته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the people of knowledge as those who know that God has power over everything.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله ، عنهما في قوله : انما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء قال : الذين يعلمون ان الله على كل شيء قدير

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge is not having many reports; it is fear of God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله ، عنه قال : ليس العلم من كثرة الحديث ، ولكن العلم من الخشية

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r3.speaker: صالح أبي الخليل
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r3.claim: Salih Abu al-Khalil says the people who know God best fear Him most.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r3.anchor: عن صالح أبي الخليل رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : انما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء قال : اعلمهم بالله اشدهم له خشية

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r4.speaker: رجل
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r4.claim: A reported saying distinguishes three scholars: one who knows God and His commands and fears Him; one who knows God and fears Him but lacks knowledge of legal limits and duties; and one who knows those rules but does not fear God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r4.anchor: من طريق سفيان ، عن أبي حيان التيمي ، عن رجل قال : كان يقال : العلماء ثلاثة عالم بالله ، وعالم بأمر الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r5.speaker: مالك بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r5.claim: Malik says knowledge is not abundant narration; it is a light God casts into the heart.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r5.anchor: عن مالك بن انس رضي الله ، عنه قال : ان العلم ليس بكثرة الرواية انما العلم نور يقذفه الله في القلب

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r6.claim: Al-Hasan defines faith as fearing God unseen, desiring what God desires, and renouncing what displeases Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3180/r6.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله ، عنه قال : الايمان : من خشي الله بالغيب ورغب فيما رغب الله فيه ، وزهد فيما اسخط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r6.claim: This clause occupies the same position as the mountain-streak clause; fronting its predicate licenses the indefinite subject, and the structure follows the preceding description.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r6.anchor: ولا يلزم أن يكون مسوغ الابتداء بالنكرة غير مفيد معنى آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r7.claim: Human color variety is broadly classed geographically as white, black, yellow, and red; Arabs use a different classification, discussed with the verse on differing languages and colors in al-Rūm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r7.anchor: واختلاف ألوان الناس منه اختلاف عام وهو ألوان أصناف البشر وهي الأبيض والأسود والأصفر والأحمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r8.claim: Min is partitive: some people differ in color, while the full set of variations covers all people, as it does animals and livestock; the compact arrangement is deliberately concise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r8.anchor: أن المختلف ألوانه بعض من الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r9.claim: The mountain and animal color clauses are nominal rather than verbal because these differences are fixed in creation, unlike water and fruit changes that recur continually.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p302/r9.anchor: بالاسمية دون الفعلية كما في الجملة السابقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r1.claim: He prefers taking كذلك as the start of a new result after the evidence: visible variety prepares for the conclusion that only the learned among humanity fear God, and that human hearts and perceptions also differ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r1.anchor: الأظهر عندي أن { كذلك } ابتداء كلام يتنزل منزلة الإخبار بالنتيجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r2.claim: The statement that only scholars fear God echoes the earlier statement that only those who fear their Lord unseen receive warning, then leads into the detailed account of reciting the Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r2.anchor: وأوثر هذا الأسلوب في الدلالة تخلصا للتنويه بأهل العلم والإيمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r3.claim: On the preferred reading, كذلك predicates an omitted subject meaning such is the variation or such is the case; a similar construction in al-Kahf supports pausing before the next clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r3.anchor: خبر لمبتدأ محذوف دل عليه المقام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r4.claim: He rejects attaching كذلك to the preceding clause as an interpretation that does not fit the Quran’s structure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r4.anchor: من توابع الكلام السابق فلا يناسب نظم القرآن لضعفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r5.claim: The restriction is relative: the ignorant polytheists do not fear God, since ignorance defines their jāhiliyya; believers of that time are the learned, whose degrees of fear still vary greatly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r5.anchor: وهم أهل الشرك فإن من أخص أوصافهم أنهم أهل الجاهلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r6.claim: God is placed before the subject because the scholars are the group exclusively described as fearing Him, so the restricted element is delayed according to the rule for exclusive constructions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r6.anchor: لأن المحصور فيهم خشية الله هم العلماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r7.claim: The scholars meant are those who know God and the religious law; knowledge of unrelated disciplines alone does not bring a person nearer to God’s fear of reward and punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r7.anchor: وعلى حسب مقدار العلم في ذلك تقوى الخشية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r8.claim: Knowledge of the law teaches its true terms, aims, and consequences; a scholar generally acts accordingly and, even when desire leads to a lapse, knows its harmful end, which prompts restraint or repentance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p304/r8.anchor: فإن هو خالف ما دعت إليه الشريعة في بعض الأحوال أو في بعض الأوقات لداعي شهوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r1.claim: A non-scholar who follows scholars acts as they do, and that person’s fear of God derives from the scholars’ fear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r1.anchor: وغير العالم إن اهتدى بالعلماء فسعيه مثل سعي العلماء وخشيته متولدة عن خشية العلماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r2.speaker: أبو محمد بن أبي زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r2.claim: Ibn Abī Zayd says knowledge guides and leads to good; those nearest to God are those who know Him best, fear Him most, and desire what is with Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو محمد بن أبي زيد ( والعلم دليل على الخيرات وقائد إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r3.claim: God’s might shows He does not need the polytheists’ faith, yet He wants good for them and accepts their repentance if they return to what He calls them to.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r3.anchor: تكميل للدلالة على استغناء الله تعالى عن إيمان المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p305/r4.claim: Following might with forgiveness softens the discouragement that divine independence could cause in potential converts and also promises forgiveness to the scholars.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r11.claim: An omitted “livestock” precedes “varied in color,” and the pronoun returns to it; animals already includes humans and livestock, but both are separately named for emphasis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r11.anchor: وقوله مختلف ألوانه قبله محذوف إليه يعود الضمير تقديره والأنعام خلق مختلف ألوانه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r12.claim: Kadhālika may close the preceding statement, making a suitable pause, or begin the next clause as its cause, as many exegetes hold.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r12.anchor: وقوله كذلك يحتمل أن يكون من الكلام الأول فيجيء الوقف عليه حسنا، وإلى هذا ذهب كثير من المفسرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r13.claim: The scholars who fear God are those who grasp the lesson and reflect on it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436#2/r13.anchor: أي المحصلون لهذه العبرة الناظرون فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r1.claim: Some commentators call fear of God the head of knowledge; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this a homiletic saying that does not withstand scrutiny.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r1.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين الخشية رأس العلم، وهذه عبارة وعظية لا تثبت عند النقد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r2.claim: He prefers the sound, consistent formulation that knowledge is the head and cause of fear of God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r2.anchor: بل الصحيح المطرد أن يقال العلم رأس الخشية، وسببها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says fear of God is the head of every wisdom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r3.anchor: ورد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال «خشية الله رأس كل حكمة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r4.claim: A second Prophetic saying identifies fear of God as the head of wisdom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r4.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «رأس الحكمة مخافة الله»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says asceticism is sufficient knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في تفسير هذه الآية كفى بالزهد علما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r6.speaker: مسروق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r6.claim: Masrūq says it is enough knowledge for a person to fear God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r6.anchor: وقال مسروق وكفى بالمرء علما أن يخشى الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r7.claim: He links the verse's fearful person to the promise that the one who fears will remember.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r8.claim: The Prophet says the one most knowledgeable about God is the one most fearful of Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r8.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أعلمكم بالله أشدكم له خشية»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r9.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r9.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says anyone who does not fear God is not a scholar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r9.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: من لم يخش الله فليس بعالم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r10.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r10.claim: An anonymous saying makes fear of God the head of wisdom in the opening of the Psalms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r10.anchor: ويقال إن فاتحة الزبور رأس الحكمة خشية الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says fear of God is sufficient knowledge, while being deluded about Him is ignorance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r11.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: كفى بخشية الله علما وبالاغترار، به جهلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r12.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r12.claim: Mujāhid and al-Shaʿbī define a true scholar as one who fears God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد والشعبي: إنما العالم من يخشى الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r13.claim: Innamā singles out scholars here without necessarily restricting the meaning exclusively; its force depends on context, as the contrasting examples of ʿAntarah and God's oneness show.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r13.anchor: وإنما في هذه الآية تخصيص العلماء لا للحصر، وهي لفظة تصلح للحصر وتأتي أيضا دونه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r14.claim: The passage as a whole proves God's oneness and power and is intended to establish the argument against Quraysh's disbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p437/r14.anchor: هذه الآية بجملتها دليل على الوحدانية والقدرة والقصد بها إقامة الحجة على كفار قريش

BURSEVI:v7p268/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268/r3.claim: Dawabb are animals that move on the earth, though the word commonly refers to riding animals such as horses, mules, and donkeys, and it can be masculine.
BURSEVI:v7p268/r3.anchor: جمع دابة وهي ما يدب على الأرض من الحيوان وغلب على ما يركب من الخيل والبغال والحمير

BURSEVI:v7p268/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268/r4.claim: An'am means camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; horses, mules, and donkeys are excluded.
BURSEVI:v7p268/r4.anchor: جمع نعم محركة وقد يسكن عينه الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز دون غيرها

BURSEVI:v7p268/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268/r5.claim: The singular pronoun in مختلف ألوانه refers to an implicit some drawn from من; some people and animals vary as white, red, or black.
BURSEVI:v7p268/r5.anchor: بأن يكون أبيض وأحمر وأسود ولم يقل هنا ألوانها لأن الضمير يعود إلى البعض الدال عليه من

BURSEVI:v7p268/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268/r6.claim: Kadhālika is a simile-forming verbal noun modifying an implied مصدر of اختلاف, and it closes the preceding clause.
BURSEVI:v7p268/r6.anchor: تم الكلام هنا وهو مصدر تشبيهي لقوله مختلف أي : صفة لمصدر مؤكد

BURSEVI:v7p268/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268/r7.claim: One who fails to recognize God's power to create things and transform them from state to state will not fear Him.
BURSEVI:v7p268/r7.anchor: هركه نداند قدرت خدايرا بر آفريدن اشيا وعالم نبود بتحويل هر يزى از حالى بحالى كونه از خداى تعالى ترسد

BURSEVI:v7p268/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268/r8.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v7p268/r8.claim: Al-Irshad links this to 35:18, identifying those who truly fear God as people who know Him and His attributes and acts; fear depends on knowledge, and the Prophet said he was most God-fearing.
BURSEVI:v7p268/r8.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" وهو تكملة لقوله تعالى : {إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب}

BURSEVI:v7p268/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268/r9.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v7p268/r9.claim: Al-Irshad explains that those deprived of knowledge of God, including the unbelievers, cannot be affected by warning; the following mention of God's acts demonstrates His power.
BURSEVI:v7p268/r9.anchor: وحيث كان الكفرة بمعزل عن هذه المعرفة امتنع إنذارهم بالكلية انتهى

BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r1.claim: Putting God, the object of fear, before العلماء restricts who fears Him to the learned; reversing the order would instead mean that they fear no one but God.
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r1.anchor: وتقديم المخشي وهو المفعول للاختصاص وحصر الفاعلية أي : لا يخشى الله من بين عباده إلا العلماء

BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة وعمر بن عبد العزيز وابن سيرين
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and Ibn Sirin read Allah in the nominative and العلماء in the accusative, using fear metaphorically for honoring: God honors the learned.
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة وعمر بن عبد العزيز وابن سيرين برفع اسم الله ونصب العلماء

BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r3.claim: Abd Allah ibn Umar takes khashya here to mean choosing, so God chooses the learned from among His servants.
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r3.anchor: وجعل عبد الله بن عمر الخشية بمعنى الاختيار أي : إنما يختار الله من بين عباده العلماء

BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r4.claim: God is mighty in exacting vengeance from one who does not fear His punishment, and forgiving toward those who fear Him; these attributes explain why He must be feared.
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r4.anchor: غالبست در انتقام كشيدن از كسى كه نترسد از عقوبت او

BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r5.claim: Fear is heartache at an expected future harm, arising either from many sins or from knowledge of God's majesty; prophetic fear belongs to the latter kind.
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r5.anchor: قيل الخشية تألم القلب بسبب توقع مكروه في المستقبل يكون تارة بكثرة الجناية من العبد

BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r6.claim: Believers should seek knowledge of God, since degrees of fear and reverent awe rise in proportion to knowledge.
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r6.anchor: فعلى المؤمن أن يجتهد في تحصيل العلم بالله حتى يكون أخشى الناس فبقدر مراتب العلم تكون مراتب الخوف والخشية

BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r7.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r7.claim: In a report attributed to the Prophet, the most knowledgeable person is the one most fearful of God; the best companion helps remembrance, the worst neither helps nor reminds, and a corrupt scholar corrupts people.
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r7.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سئل يا رسول الله أينا أعلم؟ قال : "أخشاكم

BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r8.claim: The closing Persian couplet warns that reading more without putting knowledge into practice leaves a person ignorant.
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r8.anchor: علم جندانكه بيشتر خوانى ون عمل در تونيست نادانى

BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r9.claim: Bursevī prays to be made knowledgeable and realized, and sincere in fear and reverent awe.
BURSEVI:v7p268#2/r9.anchor: نسأل الله سبحانه أن يجعلنا عالمين ومحققين وفي الخوف والخشية صادقين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r1.claim: The colors of people, animals, and livestock vary just as the fruits do.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r8.claim: The scholars meant are those who know God.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says those who know God’s might, power, and sovereignty are the ones who fear Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد إنما يخافني من خلقي من علم جبروتي وعزتي وسلطاني

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r10.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r10.claim: Mujāhid and al-Shaʿbī define a scholar as one who fears God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد والشعبي العالم من خاف الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r11.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r11.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says whoever does not fear God is not a scholar.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p485#4/r11.anchor: وقال الربيع ابن انس من لم يخش الله فليس بعالم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r1.claim: Al-dawābb means all creatures that move on legs; livestock is a specific category conjoined after the general category of animals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r1.anchor: كل ما دب على قوائم-والأنعام، من باب عطف الخاص على العام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r2.claim: People differ in complexion: Berbers and Ethiopians are very dark, Slavs and Romans very fair, Arabs lie between, and Indians are less so; animals vary even within a species or as spotted individuals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r2.anchor: فالناس منهم بربر وحبوش وطماطم في غاية السواد، وصقالبة وروم في غاية البياض، والعرب بين ذلك، والهنود دون ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r3.claim: People's differing languages and colors are signs for the worlds, as 30:22 states.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r3.anchor: في الآية الأخرى: {واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم إن في ذلك لآيات للعالمين} [الروم: 22]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r4.claim: A man asks the Prophet whether his Lord dyes; the Prophet answers that God dyes with a color that does not fade, in red, yellow, and white. The report also circulated in mursal and mawquf forms; Ibn Kathir says God knows best.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أيصبغ ربك؟ قال: "نعم صبغا لا ينفض، أحمر وأصفر وأبيض"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r5.claim: Those who truly fear God are those who know Him; more complete knowledge of the majestic, powerful, all-knowing God and His perfect attributes and names brings greater fear.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r5.anchor: كلما كانت المعرفة به أتم والعلم به أكمل، كانت الخشية له أعظم وأكثر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the scholars are those who know God is capable of all things.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r6.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} قال: الذين يعلمون أن الله على كل شيء قدير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas defines a scholar of the Merciful as one who avoids association, follows God's lawful and forbidden limits, keeps His charge, and is certain of meeting Him and answering for deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس (5) قال: العالم بالرحمن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r8.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says fear is what stands between a person and disobeying God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p544/r8.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: الخشية هي التي تحول بينك وبين معصية الله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r1.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says a scholar fears the Merciful unseen, desires what God desires, and shuns what He dislikes; he then recites this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r1.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: العالم من خشي الرحمن بالغيب، ورغب فيما رغب الله فيه، وزهد فيما سخط الله فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge is not a large quantity of transmitted reports but abundant fear of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r2.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، أنه قال: ليس العلم عن كثرة الحديث، ولكن العلم عن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r3.claim: Malik says knowledge is not numerous narrations; it is a light God places in the heart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r3.anchor: عن ابن وهب، عن مالك قال: إن العلم ليس بكثرة الرواية، وإنما العلم نور يجعله الله في القلب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r4.speaker: أحمد بن صالح المصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r4.claim: Ahmad ibn Salih explains that fear is not gained by many narrations, though obligatory knowledge comes through Qur'an, Sunna, Companions, and later imams; Malik's light means understanding and knowing meanings.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r5.speaker: رجل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r5.claim: A saying transmitted by Sufyan al-Thawri distinguishes three scholars: one knows God and His commands, one knows God but not commands, and one knows commands without fearing God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p545/r5.anchor: عن رجل قال: كان يقال: العلماء ثلاثة: عالم بالله عالم بأمر الله، وعالم بالله ليس بعالم بأمر الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r1.claim: Jabir reports that the finest Quran reciter is one whose voice makes listeners think he fears God; Ibn Majah’s connected chain is weak because Abdullah ibn Ja‘far al-Madini and his teacher are weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r1.anchor: عن جابر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن من أحسن الناس صوتا بالقرآن الذي إذا سمعتوه يقرأ حسبتموه يخشى الله "

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r2.claim: The legally desired beautification of the voice should prompt reflection, understanding, humility, submission, and obedience; Quran should be kept clear of invented, entertaining musical modes and rhythms.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r2.anchor: أن المطلوب شرعا إنما هو التحسين بالصوت الباعث على تدبر القرآن وتفهمه والخشوع والخضوع والانقياد للطاعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r3.claim: A report from Hudhayfa commands reciting in Arab voices and avoiding the styles of sinners and scriptural communities; later people will perform the Quran as musical song, monastic chant, and lament, without it passing their throats, while their hearts and admirers are captivated.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r3.anchor: عن حذيفة بن اليمان قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "اقرؤوا القرآن بلحون العرب وأصواتها، وإياكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r4.speaker: عليم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r4.claim: A companion, whom Yazid thinks was Abis al-Ghifari, saw people fleeing plague and wished to die first; he cited Prophetic warnings of selling judgment, trivializing blood, severing kinship, and appointing Quran singers for their performance rather than learning or virtue. Two further traits are omitted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p64/r4.anchor: عن عليم قال: " كنا على سطح ومعنا رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. قال يزيد: لا أعلمه إلا قال: عابس الغفاري

JISHUMI:v8p5843/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r6.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r6.claim: The general reading has العلماء nominative: the learned fear God’s punishment and therefore obey Him.
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r6.anchor: قراءة العامة: (العلماء) بالرفع، يعني: أنهم يخافون عقاب الله فيطيعونه

JISHUMI:v8p5843/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r7.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز وأبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r7.claim: A variant reported from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and similarly from Abu Hanifa puts العلماء in the accusative and construes يخشى as “knows” or, in one explanation, “chooses”; the author rejects it as nonstandard, treating the attribution as hypothetical.
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r7.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز: يخشى الله رفعا العلماء نصبا، وروي نحوه عن أبي حنيفة، على أن معنى (يخشى) يعلم، وقيل: يختار

JISHUMI:v8p5843/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r8.claim: The accusative reading is not accepted as a recitation because it conflicts with the widely transmitted reading; the reports are treated as saying only that it would make sense hypothetically.
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r8.anchor: ولا تجوز القراءة به؛ لأنه خلاف المستفيض، ويحمل على أنهما قالا: لو قرئ به لكان يصح في المعنى

JISHUMI:v8p5844/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5844/r2.speaker: المؤرج
JISHUMI:v8p5844/r2.claim: Al-Muʾarrij explains the masculine pronoun in مختلف ألوانه by the preceding من.
JISHUMI:v8p5844/r2.anchor: وقوله: (مختلف ألوانه) ذكر الكناية لأجل (من)، عن المؤرج

JISHUMI:v8p5844/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5844/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5844/r7.claim: The pronoun in ألوانه can refer to the varied colors of people, animals, and livestock in what God created, parallel to the preceding creations.
JISHUMI:v8p5844/r7.anchor: وقيل: ذكر الكناية في (ألوانه)؛ لأن تقديره: فيما خلقنا مختلف ألوانه من الناس والدواب والأنعام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r16.claim: A variant lightens al-dawābb; like al-ḍāllīn, the readings avoid meeting two vowelless consonants, one moving the first and the other deleting the last.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r16.anchor: وقرىء : ( والدواب ) مخففا ونظير هذا التخفيف قراءة من قرأ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r17.claim: “Likewise” points back to variety in fruits and mountains.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r17.anchor: وقوله : { كذالك } أي كاختلاف الثمرات والجبال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r18.claim: Those who know God know His attributes, justice, oneness, and what is possible or impossible for Him; they honor and fear Him as He deserves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r18.anchor: والمراد : العلماء به الذين علموه بصفاته وعدله وتوحيده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r19.claim: The more one knows God, the more one fears Him; the less one knows Him, the more secure one feels.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p618#2/r19.anchor: ومن ازداد به علما ازداد منه خوفا ، ومن كان علمه به أقل كان آمن

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r11.claim: One explanation says the colors are white, red, and black.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r11.anchor: كذلك مختلف ألوانه أبيض وأحمر وأسود

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r12.claim: Alternatively, as fruits, mountains, people, animals, and livestock vary in color, servants differ in reverent fear.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r12.anchor: كما اختلف ألوان الثمار والجبال والناس والدواب والأنعام كذلك تختلف أحوال العباد في الخشية

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r13.claim: Here العلماء means people who fear God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r14.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r14.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says whoever does not fear God is not a scholar.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r14.anchor: قال الربيع بن أنس : من لم يخش الله فليس بعالم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r15.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r15.claim: Ibn Masud says the God-fearing are masters and scholars are leaders.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r15.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : المتقون سادة , والعلماء قادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r16.speaker: قيل
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r16.claim: A saying identifies the Psalms' opening wisdom as fear of God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p470/r16.anchor: وقيل : فاتحة الزبور الحكمة خشية الله

MUQATIL:35:25-28/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:25-28/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:25-28/r9.claim: People, crawling creatures, and livestock vary in color—white, red, yellow, and black—as the fruits do.
MUQATIL:35:25-28/r9.anchor: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام } بيض وحمر وصفر وسود

MUQATIL:35:25-28/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:25-28/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:25-28/r10.claim: The wording has fronting; those who know God are the people who fear Him most.
MUQATIL:35:25-28/r10.anchor: فيها تقديم يقول: أشد الناس لله عز وجل خيفة أعلمهم الله تعالى

MUQATIL:35:25-28/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:25-28/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:25-28/r11.claim: God is mighty in His dominion and forgiving of believers’ sins.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r1.claim: The construction means some among people, animals, and livestock vary in color.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r2.claim: Their colors vary like fruits and mountains; after listing signs of power and craft in diverse creation, the passage turns to those who fear God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r2.anchor: أى كاختلاف الثمرات والجبال ولما قال ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء وعدد آيات الله واعلام قدرته وآثار صنعته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r3.claim: Scholars who fear God know Him through His attributes and revere Him; greater knowledge brings greater fear, while lesser knowledge brings greater ease.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r3.anchor: أى العلماء به الذين علموه بصفاته فعظموه ومن ازداد علما به ازداد منه خوفا ومن كان علمه به أقل كان آمن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r4.claim: A hadith says the most knowledgeable of people about God are the most fearful of Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r4.anchor: وفى الحديث أعلمكم بالله اشدكم له خشية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r5.claim: Putting God's name before scholars means the ones who fear among His servants are scholars; reversing the order would mean they fear none but God.
