NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r5.anchor: وتقديم اسم الله تعالى وتأخير العلماء يؤذن ان معناه ان الذين يخشون من عباده العلماء دون غيرهم ولو عكس لكان المعنى أنهم لا يخشون إلا الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة وابن عبد العزيز وابن سيرين
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa, Ibn Abd al-Aziz, and Ibn Sirin read the verb passively, yielding the sense that scholars revere God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة وابن عبد العزيز وابن سرين رضى الله عنهم إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء والخشية في هذه القراءة استعارة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r7.claim: God's power to punish and His forgiveness and reward for the obedient explain why He must be feared.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p342#3/r7.anchor: تعليل لوجوب الخشية لدلالته على عقوبة العصاة وقهرهم وإثابة أهل الطاعة والعفو عنهم

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r12.claim: A lightened reading parallels al-dallin: adjacent quiescent letters are avoided by moving one or deleting one.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r12.anchor: فحرك ذلك أولهما، وحذف هذا آخرهما قاله الزمخشري.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r13.claim: People, animals, and livestock have red, white, black, and other colors, evidencing a choosing Maker.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r13.anchor: أي فيهم الأحمر والأبيض والأسود وغير ذلك، وكل ذلك دليل على صانع مختار.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r14.speaker: المؤرج
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r14.claim: Al-Muʾarrij says the masculine pronoun observes the collective man, ‘whoever.’
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r14.anchor: وقال: «مختلف ألوانه» فذكر الضمير مراعاة ل«من» قاله المؤرج.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r15.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r15.claim: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash refers the pronoun to an implicit ma: some among them have different colors.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28/r15.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن عياش: إنما ذكر الكناية لأجل أنها مردودة إلى «ما» مضمرة

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r4.claim: Kadhālika closes the preceding point about variation in servants’ fear; the scholars’ statement begins anew.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r4.anchor: } هنا تمام الكلام أي كذلك تختلف أحوال العباد في الخشية، ثم استأنف فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r5.claim: Scholars fear God’s power; knowing He is capable makes them certain He punishes disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r5.anchor: يعني بالعلماء الذين يخافون قدرته فمن علم أنه عز وجل قدير أيقن بمعاقبته على المعصية

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says scholars know God has power over everything.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r6.anchor: كما روى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس «إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء» قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r7.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas says one who does not fear God is no scholar.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r7.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: من لم يخش الله تعالى فليس بعالم.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r8.claim: Mujahid says the scholar is the one who fears God.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إنما العالم من خشي الله عز وجل.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿud says fear of God is sufficient knowledge and delusion is ignorance.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r9.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود: كفى بخشية الله تعالى علما وبالاغترار جهلا.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r10.speaker: سعد بن إبراهيم
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r10.claim: Asked who was most learned in Medina, Saʿd ibn Ibrahim answered: the most God-fearing.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r10.anchor: وقيل لسعد بن إبراهيم: من أفقه أهل المدينة؟ قال أتقاهم لربه عز وجل.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r11.claim: Mujahid also says the jurist is one who fears God.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r11.anchor: وعن مجاهد قال: إنما الفقيه من يخاف الله عز وجل.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r12.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r12.claim: ʿAli defines jurisprudence as balancing hope and warning, adhering to Qurʾan, and pairing worship with knowledge, understanding, and reflection.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r12.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه قال: إن الفقيه حق الفقيه من لم يقنط الناس من رحمة الله

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r13.claim: Al-Darimi transmits a mursal report through Mak'hul: scholars outrank worshippers and creation prays for teachers of good.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r13.anchor: أسند الدارمي أبو محمد عن مكحول قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r14.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r14.claim: Kaʿb warns of people who learn without acting and seek worldly gain through religion, then face a confounding trial.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r14.anchor: أنه سمع تبيعا يحدث عن كعب قال: إني لأجد نعت قوم

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r15.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r15.claim: Al-Tirmidhi also transmits the warning as a raised report from Abu al-Darda; no grading is given here.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r15.anchor: خرجه الترمذي مرفوعا من حديث أبي الدرداء

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r16.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز وأبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r16.claim: A reading attributed to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz and related from Abu Hanifa makes Allah nominative and scholars accusative.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r16.anchor: فإن قلت: فما وجه قراءة من قرأ «إنما يخشى الله» بالرفع «من عباده العلماء» بالنصب، وهو عمر بن عبد العزيز

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r17.claim: Zamakhshari reads it figuratively: people revere scholars as they revere an imposing, feared man.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r17.anchor: الزمخشري: فإن قلت: فما وجه قراءة من قرأ

QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:27-28#2/r18.claim: God’s might and forgiveness explain the duty of fear: He punishes sinners, rewards the obedient, and pardons.

RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r1.claim: The verse continues evidence for God's power and will by surveying composite creation: animals and non-animals, with plants nobler than minerals, followed by animals; the earlier mention of fruit and mountains represents plants and minerals.
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r1.anchor: قسم دلائل الخلق في العالم الذي نحن فيه وهو عالم المركبات

RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r2.claim: Humans head the animal list as its noblest kind. Beasts precede livestock either because their benefits are enjoyed while alive whereas livestock are eaten, or because “beast” conventionally includes the horse, nobler than other animals after humans.
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r2.anchor: لأن منافعها في حياتها والأنعام منفعتها في الأكل منها

RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r3.claim: The masculine singular description is used because humans are included among the subjects, and masculine wording is more elevated and apt.
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r3.anchor: فذكر لكون الإنسان من جملة المذكورين

RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r4.claim: Fear of the one feared grows with knowledge of him: the scholar knows God and therefore fears and hopes in him.
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r4.anchor: الخشية بقدر معرفة المخشي ، والعالم يعرف الله فيخافه ويرجوه

RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r5.claim: Scholars outrank worshippers because honor is measured by piety (49:13), and piety in turn by knowledge; honor thus depends on knowledge rather than deeds, though a scholar's failure to act calls his knowledge into question.

RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r6.claim: God's might and retribution evoke complete fear, while his forgiving what is lesser evokes abundant hope.
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r6.anchor: كونه عزيزا ذا انتقام يوجب الخوف التام ، وكونه غفورا لما دون ذلك يوجب الرجاء البالغ

RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p19#3/r7.claim: In the reading that puts “scholars” in the accusative and “God” in the nominative, the sense is that God is magnified and revered.

STUDYQURAN:35:28/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r1.claim: IK reads the different colors as the diversity of human races and ethnicities, linked to 30:22.
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r1.anchor: the variation in your tongues and colors (IK)

STUDYQURAN:35:28/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r2.claim: Q also reads the differences as variations in people’s inner states.
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r2.anchor: inner states of human beings differ (Q)

STUDYQURAN:35:28/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r3.speaker: IK, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r3.claim: IK, Q, and Ṭ take those who know to mean those who know that God has power over all things.
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r3.anchor: God is Powerful over all things (IK, Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:35:28/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r4.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that the person with the greatest knowledge of God fears Him most intensely.
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r4.anchor: The Prophet is reported to have said, “The one among you

STUDYQURAN:35:28/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r5.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r5.claim: R takes the verse to show that knowledge is superior to worship.
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r5.anchor: the superiority of knowledge over worship (R)

STUDYQURAN:35:28/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r6.speaker: ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r6.claim: A famous hadith says the knowledge seeker is guided toward the Garden, angels and creatures seek forgiveness for the learned, and the learned inherit prophetic knowledge and outrank worshippers.
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r6.anchor: as in a famous ḥadīth: “Whosoever sets upon a path to seek knowledge, God will set him upon a path to the Garden.

STUDYQURAN:35:28/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r7.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r7.claim: Bḍ notes that the following mention of obligatory worship shows knowledge must be joined to worship and embodied in action to benefit its possessor.
STUDYQURAN:35:28/r7.anchor: demonstrates that such knowledge must be combined with worship and manifest in one’s actions in order to be of benefit (Bḍ)

QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r1.claim: All creatures are alike in kind yet varied, which proves the existence of their Creator with the attribute of majesty.
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r1.anchor: بل جميع المخلوقات متجانس الأعيان مختلف

QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r2.claim: Innama marks emphasis and restriction: whoever lacks knowledge of God has no fear of Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r2.anchor: كلمة تحقيق تجري من وجه مجرى التحديد

QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r3.claim: Rahba is fear that drives a person to flee, whereas khashya restrains the person and keeps them with God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r3.anchor: الفرق بين الخشية والرهبة أن الرهبة خوف يوجب هرب صاحبه

QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r4.claim: Fear follows faith, khashya follows knowledge, and awe follows gnosis.

QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r5.claim: Reported explanations say scholars fear falling short in God's due and feel modest before His awareness.
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r5.anchor: ويقال خشية العلماء من تقصيرهم في أداء حقه

QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r6.claim: A further explanation is that scholars fear bad manners, disrespect, untimely familiarity in speech, or leaving what is better.
QUSHAYRI:v3p67/r6.anchor: ويقال حذرا من أن يحصل لهم سوء أدب وترك احترام

TAB-FULL:v19p364/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p364/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p364/r1.claim: Like fruits and mountains, people, animals, and livestock differ in color, including red, white, black, and yellow.
TAB-FULL:v19p364/r1.anchor: هو الأسود، يعني لونه كما اختلف ألوان هذه اختلف ألوان الناس والدواب والأنعام كذلك

TAB-FULL:v19p364/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p364/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p364/r2.claim: Qatada lists red, green, and yellow fruit, white mountain tracks, red and white mountains, and black mountains; people and animals vary likewise.
TAB-FULL:v19p364/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به ثمرات مختلفا ألوانها} [فاطر: 27] " أحمر وأخضر وأضفر

TAB-FULL:v19p364/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p364/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v19p364/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says mountains have white, red, and black tracks, and people likewise have varied colors.
TAB-FULL:v19p364/r3.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ومن الجبال جدد بيض} [فاطر: 27] «طرائق بيض، وحمر وسود، وكذلك الناس مختلف ألوانهم»

TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r1.claim: Scholars fear God and guard against punishment through obedience because they know His power and will and expect punishment for disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} [فاطر: 28] قال: «الذين يعلمون أن الله على كل شيء قدير»

TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies scholars as those who know God is capable of all things.
TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} [فاطر: 28] قال: «الذين يعلمون أن الله على كل شيء قدير»

TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r3.claim: Qatada transmits the maxim that fear is sufficient knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v19p364#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} [فاطر: 28] قال: " كان يقال: كفى بالرهبة علما

SULAMI:v2p160#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r1.claim: Reverent fear is more complete than ordinary fear because it is the quality of scholars and saints.
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : الخشية أتم من الخوف لأنه صفة العلماء

SULAMI:v2p160#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r2.claim: For scholars, reverent fear means avoiding breaches of respect in worship, speaking about God, following the Messenger, and serving saints and the truthful.
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : خشية العلماء من ترك الحرمة في العبادات وترك الحرمة

SULAMI:v2p160#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r3.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r3.claim: Scholarly reverence includes restraint from being overly familiar in supplication and asking.
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r3.anchor: قال النصرآباذي : خشية العلماء من الانبساط في الدعاء والسؤال

SULAMI:v2p160#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r4.claim: Scholars are the most compassionate of people because of their fear of God and concern for what He taught them.
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r4.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه أرحم الناس العلماء لخشيتهم من الله

SULAMI:v2p160#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r5.speaker: الحارث
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r5.claim: Knowledge produces reverence, renunciation produces rest, and gnosis produces turning back to God.
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحارث : العلم يورث الخشية والزهد يورث الراحة ،

SULAMI:v2p160#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r6.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r6.claim: Reverence begins with knowledge, then proceeds through veneration, glorification, awe, and annihilation; once effaced, the servant flees until forgetting his own acts.
SULAMI:v2p160#2/r6.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : أوائل الخشية العلم ثم الاجلال

TABATABAI:35:27-28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:27-28/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:27-28/r1.claim: After discussing prophethood and revealed books, the passage returns to signs of divine unity and turns to the revealed Book’s truth and effects.
TABATABAI:35:27-28/r1.anchor: بيان رجوع إلى ذكر آيات أخر من آيات التوحيد وفيها انتقال إلى حديث الكتاب وأنه حق نازل من عند الله

TABATABAI:35:28-30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r1.claim: Among people, crawling creatures, and livestock such as camels, sheep, and cattle, some have white, red, or black colors, like fruits and mountains.
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r1.anchor: ومن الناس والدواب التي تدب في الأرض والأنعام كالإبل والغنم والبقر بعض مختلف ألوانه بالبياض والحمرة والسواد

TABATABAI:35:28-30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r2.claim: One parsing treats kathālika as the predicate of an omitted subject: the situation is thus, summarizing the preceding detail about the varied colors.
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r2.anchor: وقيل قوله { كذلك } خبر لمبتدأ محذوف، والتقدير الأمر كذلك فهو تقرير إجمالي للتفصيل المتقدم

TABATABAI:35:28-30/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r3.claim: A further parsing attaches kathālika to yakhshā, meaning the learned fear God by reflecting on these signs; the author finds this remote in wording and meaning.
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r3.anchor: وقيل { كذلك } متعلق بقوله { يخشى } في قوله { إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء } والإشارة إلى ما تقدم

TABATABAI:35:28-30/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r4.claim: The sentence explains that reflecting on the signs produces true faith and complete fear of God in the learned, not the ignorant, and clarifies the warning’s successful recipients in 35:18.
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r4.anchor: إنما يؤثر أثره ويورث الإيمان بالله حقيقة والخشية منه بتمام معنى الكلمة في العلماء دون الجهال

TABATABAI:35:28-30/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r5.claim: The learned are those who fully know God’s names, attributes, and acts; their hearts are reassured, doubt and anxiety recede, and their deeds match their words.
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r5.anchor: الذين يعرفون الله سبحانه بأسمائه وصفاته وأفعاله معرفة تامة تطمئن بها قلوبهم وتزيل وصمة الشك والقلق عن نفوسهم

TABATABAI:35:28-30/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r6.claim: Here fear means true, complete reverence, producing inward awe and outward humility.
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r6.anchor: والمراد بالخشية حينئذ حق الخشية ويتبعها خشوع في باطنهم وخضوع في ظاهرهم

TABATABAI:35:28-30/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r7.claim: God’s might explains why the learned fear Him: He is wholly dominant and cannot be overcome; His abundant forgiveness explains their trust, devotion, and longing to meet Him.
TABATABAI:35:28-30/r7.anchor: لعزته تعالى وكونه قاهرا غير مقهور وغالبا غير مغلوب من كل جهة يخشاه العارفون

TABRISI:35:27-28/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:27-28/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:27-28/r5.claim: Mukhtalifan is an adjective of fruits, while “their colors differ” is a predicate of an omitted subject, understood as “it is diverse in color.”
TABRISI:35:27-28/r5.anchor: مختلفا صفة لثمرات وألوانها مرفوع بأنه فاعله مختلف ألوانه خبر مبتدأ محذوف

TABRISI:35:27-28/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:27-28/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:27-28/r6.claim: The pronoun in “its colors” may refer to the understood subject or to a described kind; the author prefers the latter analysis, “a kind diverse in color.”
TABRISI:35:27-28/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الهاء عائدا إلى موصوف لمختلف تقدير جنس مختلف ألوانه وهو الأصح

TABRISI:35:27-28/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:27-28/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:27-28/r14.claim: People, land animals, and livestock—such as camels, sheep, and cattle—also have varied colors, like fruits and mountains.

TABRISI:35:27-28/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:27-28/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:27-28/r15.claim: Only scholars who truly know God fear Him with proper fear and guard against His disobedience and punishment.
TABRISI:35:27-28/r15.anchor: أي ليس يخاف الله حق خوفه ولا يحذر معاصيه خوفا من نقمته إلا العلماء

TABRISI:35:27-28/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:27-28/r16.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:35:27-28/r16.claim: Al-Sadiq says scholars are those whose deeds confirm their words; whoever’s deeds fail to match his words is not a scholar.
TABRISI:35:27-28/r16.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع أنه قال: يعني بالعلماء من صدق قوله فعله

TABRISI:35:27-28/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:27-28/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:35:27-28/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says those among creation who fear God are those who know His might, grandeur, and sovereignty.
TABRISI:35:27-28/r17.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: يريد إنما يخافني من خلقي من علم جبروتي وعزتي

THALABI:v8p104#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p104#2/r11.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v8p104#2/r11.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the order means black, deeply black; gharābīb is the plural of gharīb, a blackness likened to a crow.
THALABI:v8p104#2/r11.anchor: قال الفراء: فيه تقديم وتأخير، مجازه: سود غرابيب، وهي جمع غربيب، هو الشديد السواد يشبهها بلون الغراب

THALABI:v8p105/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p105/r2.speaker: المؤرخ
THALABI:v8p105/r2.claim: Al-Muʾarrikh explains the form ألوانه by the preceding من.

THALABI:v8p105/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p105/r3.speaker: محمد بن عياش
THALABI:v8p105/r3.claim: Ibn Ayyash explains ألوانه as referring back to an implicit ما: among people, beasts, and cattle, there is what varies in color.
THALABI:v8p105/r3.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر محمد بن عياش يقول: إنما قال: ألوانه لأجل أنها مردودة إلى «ما» في الإضمار، مجازه:

THALABI:v8p105/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p105/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p105/r4.claim: Likewise concludes the preceding statement about variation, and a new sentence begins with God being feared by the learned.
THALABI:v8p105/r4.anchor: كذلك تمام الكلام هاهنا، أي ومن هذه الأشياء مختلف ألوانه باختلاف الثمرات، ثم ابتدأ فقال سبحانه وتعالى:

THALABI:v8p105/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p105/r5.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
THALABI:v8p105/r5.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz read God as nominative and the learned as accusative; Abu Hanifa reportedly selected this, understood as God knowing—or choosing—the learned, but the author endorses the common reading as correct.
THALABI:v8p105/r5.anchor: روى عن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه قرأ (إنما يخشى الله) رفعا و (العلماء) نصبا، وهو اختيار أبي حنيفة على معنى يعلم الله، وقيل: يختار، والقراءة الصحيحة ما عليه العامة.

THALABI:v8p105/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p105/r6.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
THALABI:v8p105/r6.claim: A report raised from Ata al-Khurasani says the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr after his fear became apparent; the Prophet spoke with him, and the report says those most knowledgeable of God fear Him most.
THALABI:v8p105/r6.anchor: حدثنا عباس بن عوسجة عن عطاء الخراساني رفع الحديث قال: ظهر من أبي بكر خوف حتى عرف فيه فكلمه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ذلك فأنزل الله سبحانه تعالى:

THALABI:v8p105/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p105/r7.speaker: مسروق
THALABI:v8p105/r7.claim: Masruq says fearing God is sufficient evidence of a person's knowledge, while self-admiration over one's knowledge shows ignorance.
THALABI:v8p105/r7.anchor: وقال مسروق: كفى بالمرء علما أن يخشى الله، وكفى بالمرء جهلا أن يعجب بعلمه.

THALABI:v8p105/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p105/r8.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v8p105/r8.claim: Al-Shaʿbi defines the learned person as one who fears God.
THALABI:v8p105/r8.anchor: فقال: العالم من خشي الله عز وجل.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r3.claim: The preceding mountain-color statement ends at kadhālika, meaning that mountains differ in color.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r3.anchor: وتمام الكلام عند قوله: {كذلك} يقول: من الجبال مختلف ألوانها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r4.claim: The colors of people, animals, and livestock differ likewise, as do the colors of fruits.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r4.anchor: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام مختلف ألوانه كذلك} أي كاختلاف الثمرات.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r5.claim: The clause about the scholars fearing God begins a new sentence.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#6/r5.anchor: ثم يبتدئ: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj supplies an ellipsis: among what God created are people, animals, and livestock of differing colors, as with the fruits and mountains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: المعنى: وفيما خلقنا مختلفا ألوانه من الناس والدواب والأنعام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say the clause uses fronting and postponement, placing the object before the subject.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: في هذه الآية تقديم وتأخير (¬2). يعنيان تقديم المفعول على الفاعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says those who fear God are the people who know His omnipotence, might, and sovereignty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد إنما يخافني من خلقي من علم جبروتي وعزتي وسلطاني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r4.claim: Muqātil says those who know God best fear Him most.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أشد الناس لله خشية أعلمهم به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī says the scholars of God are the people who fear Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: العلماء بالله هم الذين يخشونه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says fear of God suffices as knowledge, while feeling secure from God is ignorance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r6.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: كفى بخشية الله علما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r7.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r7.claim: Mujāhid and al-Shaʿbī define a scholar as one who fears God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد والشعبي: العالم من خاف الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil say God is mighty in His dominion and forgiving toward believers’ sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p421/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: عزيز في ملكه، غفور لذنوب المؤمنين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:27-32/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:27-32/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:27-32/r3.claim: Humans, animals, and livestock vary in color just as mountains and fruits do.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:27-32/r3.anchor: أي: كاختلاف الجبال والثمرات في اختلاف الألوان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:27-32/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:27-32/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:27-32/r4.claim: Those who know God are the ones who fear Him intensely.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:27-32/r4.anchor: من كان عالما بالله اشتدت خشيته

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r2.claim: The colors of people, animals, and livestock differ just as the colors of the fruits and mountains differ; after this comparison the discourse breaks and resumes with the scholars’ fear of God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r2.anchor: {ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام مختلف ألوانه كذلك} [فاطر: 28] ، أي: كما اختلفت ألوان ما ذكر من الثمار والجبال، ثم انقطع الكلام، ثم استأنف

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r3.claim: The scholars who fear God are the believers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r3.anchor: ثم استأنف فقال: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} [فاطر: 28] وهم المؤمنون.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the scholars know that God has power over all things.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r4.anchor: وبلغني أن ابن عباس، قال: يعلمون أن الله على كل شيء قدير.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge is not the narration of hadith; knowledge is fear of God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r5.anchor: وحدثني قرة بن خالد، عن عون بن عبد الله بن عتبة، عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: ليس العلم رواية الحديث ولكن العلم الخشية.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r6.claim: Yahya takes Ibn Masud’s statement to mean that whoever fears God is a scholar.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p786/r6.anchor: قال يحيى: نراه أنه، يعني: أنه من خشي الله فهو عالم.

ELMALILI:35:27-31/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r8.claim: The varied human, animal, and livestock manifestations include outward and inward distinctions; some people possess knowledge and others do not.
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r8.anchor: Bunlar da öyle sûrî ve mânevî mazhariyetlere ayrılarak seçilmişlerdir. Öyle ki insanlar içinde ilmi olanlar, olmayanlar vardır

ELMALILI:35:27-31/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r9.claim: Only scholars who know Allah truly feel awe, fear, and reverence of Him.
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r9.anchor: fakat Allah haşyetini, Allah korkusunu, Allah saygısını kulları içinden ancak ulemâ duyar ancak Allah’ı bilenler o saygıyı hissederler

ELMALILI:35:27-31/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r10.claim: As 35:18 says, those continually fearing their Lord unseen benefit from the Prophet’s warning and thereby purify and protect themselves; these know Allah.
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r10.anchor: buyurulduğu üzere Allah saygısını müstemirren duyup da Peygamber’in inzârından müstefid olacak ve binâen‘aleyh temizlenip korunacak olanlar

ELMALILI:35:27-31/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r11.claim: Reverence is proportionate to knowledge of someone’s rank; the more complete a servant’s knowledge of Allah, the more complete the servant’s awe.
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r11.anchor: Çünkü bir şey hakkında saygı onun şânına olan bilgi ve bilginin derecesiyle mütenâsib olur.

ELMALILI:35:27-31/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r12.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r12.claim: The Prophet said that he was the one among them most fearful of Allah and most pious.
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r12.anchor: Onun için Resûlullah [^6] أَنَا أَخْشَاكُمْ لِل َّهِ وَأَتـْقَاكُمْ demiştir.

ELMALILI:35:27-31/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r13.claim: Allah’s being both Mighty and Forgiving prevents complacency: He cannot be overcome and can punish or destroy as He wills, so forgiveness coexists with severe retribution.
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r13.anchor: Sade bir Gafûr olsa idi, O’nu bilmek belki nazlanmaya, mağrur olmaya, hiç korkusuz ümid bağlamaya[^7] sebep olabilirdi. Fakat Allah yalnız Gafûr Rahîm değil, Azîz

ELMALILI:35:27-31/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r14.claim: The scholars’ greater awe is accompanied by greater hope in Allah.
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r14.anchor: Bununla beraber ulemânın saygısı, haşyeti, korkusu ne kadar yüksek olursa ümidi de o nisbette çok olacağı unutulmamalıdır.

ELMALILI:35:27-31/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r21.claim: Since scholars have the greatest awe of Allah, they are the most honored of His servants; the rank of knowledge is the highest.
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r21.anchor: Allah’a en çok haşyeti olan ulemâ olunca Allah’ın kulları içinde en çok tekrim buyurduğu da ulemâ olmuş olur. Bu haysiyetledir ki

ELMALILI:35:27-31/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r22.claim: Knowledge matters in practice as well as theory: the author connects knowledge and awe to the statement that righteous action raises one’s standing in 35:10.
ELMALILI:35:27-31/r22.anchor: burada da haşyet ve meşkûriyetin bu haysiyete ibtinâsı gösterilmektedir

MAJAZ:v2p154/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p154/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p154/r4.claim: The phrase distributes the description across these groups: among people, beasts, and livestock, each group has varied colors; here dawābb excludes people and camels, unlike its broad use in 11:6.
MAJAZ:v2p154/r4.anchor: مجازة: من هؤلاء جميع مختلف ألوانه ومن أولئك جميع، كذاك وقد جاءت

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r1.claim: The verses direct attention to nature's grandeur, the diversity arising from one source, and the power that produces it, emphasizing colors and kinds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r1.anchor: Dikkatlerimizi bir yandan tabiatın ihtişamına diğer yandan da bu muhteşem görünümü meydana getiren farklılıkların tek kaynaktan neşet ettiğine ve bunu sağlayan yüce kudrete çeken bu âyetlerde renk ve tür faktörüne ağırlık verildiği görülmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r4.claim: Closer study shows that colors are not the only differences: people, mountains, plants, and animals differ in many traits, all of which point to the single will and power behind their harmonious diversity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r4.anchor: İnsanlar, dağlar, bitkiler, hayvanlar renk renk olduğu gibi daha pek çok özellik ve yetenek farklarıyla da birbirlerinden ayırt edilirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r6.claim: Here khashya means awe before God's greatness, a fear arising from concern over failing to give Him His due rather than fear of harm.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r6.anchor: 28. âyette haşyet kökünden gelen ve “büyüklüğü karşısında heyecan duyarlar” diye çevirdiğimiz kelime burada, “büyüklük karşısında duyulan heyecan ve korku, zarar görmekten değil, hakkını verememekten kaynaklanan endişe” mânasına gelmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r7.claim: The Qur'an's invitation to discover the intricacies of nature makes its emphasis on the value of knowing especially striking.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r7.anchor: Muhataplarını doğadaki muhteşem görünümlerden hareketle akıllara durgunluk verecek incelikleri keşfetmeye yönlendiren Kur’an’ın, bu bağlamda bilmenin değerine vurgu yapması oldukça ilginçtir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r8.claim: The roots of ulamā include deep recognition, grasping a thing's nature, certainty, and penetrating the truth of a matter.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r8.anchor: kök anlamları arasında, bir şeyi derinlemesine tanıyıp mahiyetini idrak etme, bir konuda kesin bilgiye ulaşma, bir işin hakikatine nüfuz etme mânalarının bulunduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r9.claim: The people singled out for reverence are not merely professional scientists or memorizers; they draw conclusions from signs of God's power in the universe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r9.anchor: kendilerine gönderme yapılan ve Allah’a saygı duyma hususunda ön plana çıkarılan kişilerin, meslek olarak bilimsel faaliyet icra edenler veya birtakım bilgileri öğrenip belleklerine yerleştirmiş olanlar değil

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r10.speaker: sahâbe ve tâbiîn büyükleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r10.claim: Reports from many leading Companions and Successors say that people who make no progress in reverence for God are not truly learned, however much they know.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r10.anchor: sahâbe ve tâbiîn büyüklerinin birçoğundan yapılan rivayetlerde ne kadar bilgili olurlarsa olsunlar Allah’a saygı yolunda mesafe alamamış kimselerin âlim olarak nitelenemeyecekleri belirtilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r11.claim: Research across sciences can lead even atheists or doubters to observe cosmic balance, precise design, and harmony and to acknowledge divine power or their helplessness before it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r11.anchor: bilim dallarına mensup bilim adamlarından pek çoğunun –başlangıçta ateist veya Allah inancı konusunda mütereddit olsalar bile– bu araştırmalar sonucunda kâinattaki şaşmaz dengeyi, akılları zorlayan ince hesapları ve hayranlık uyandıran âhengi müşahede ederek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r12.claim: People previously indifferent to religion may reconsider life's meaning after seeing research results and the order of existence, which cannot be an accident.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r12.anchor: sosyal çevrenin etkisiyle dine karşı kayıtsız kalmış ve metafizik konularıyla ilgilenme fırsatı bulamamış birçok insanın az önce sözü edilen araştırmaların sonuçlarını izleyince düşünce dünyalarında önemli değişikliklerin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r13.claim: The verses remind Muslims that taking a leading role in the pursuit of knowledge is part of their religious duty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r13.anchor: Kur’an’a gönül vermiş kişilere önemli bir görevi yani ilim yolunda öncülük etmenin de Müslümanlığın gereklerinden olduğunu hatırlatmış olmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r14.claim: Following Razi, the author renders dābb as ‘riding animals’ and anʿām as ‘animals whose meat is eaten.’
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:27/r14.anchor: Râzî’nin açıklaması esas alınarak, 28. âyette geçen ve “hayvanlar” anlamına gelen devvâb ve en‘âm kelimelerinden birincisine meâlde “binek hayvanları” ikincisine “eti yenen hayvanlar” mânası verilmiştir

BURHAN:v1p341/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p341/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p341/r1.claim: Parsing anomalous readings is often more technically demanding than parsing famous readings; al-Muhtasib is useful but incomplete, while al-Ukbari's work is broader.
BURHAN:v1p341/r1.anchor: وتوجيه القراءة الشاذة أقوى في الصناعة من توجيه المشهورة

BURHAN:v1p341/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p341/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p341/r4.claim: The anomalous reading is defensible if خشية here means reverential awe and glorification rather than fear.
BURHAN:v1p341/r4.anchor: وتأويله أن الخشية هنا بمعنى الإجلال والتعظيم لا الخوف

BURHAN:v4p78/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p78/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p78/r1.claim: Words that seem synonymous fit different contexts; khashya is stronger than khawf, which signals deficiency rather than total loss, so interpretation should preserve contextual distinctions.
BURHAN:v4p78/r1.anchor: فمن ذلك الخوف والخشية لايكاد اللغوي يفرق بينهما

BURHAN:v4p78/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p78/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p78/r2.claim: Khashya arises from the greatness of the one feared even when the fearer is strong; khawf arises from the fearer's weakness even when the danger is slight.
BURHAN:v4p78/r2.anchor: بان الخشية تكون من عظم المخشى وان كان الخاشي قويا والخوف يكون من ضعف الخائف

BURHAN:v4p78/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p78/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p78/r3.claim: The contrast ‘they revere their Lord and fear the bad reckoning’ reflects God's greatness; one who understands accounting and examines himself may not fear the reckoning.
BURHAN:v4p78/r3.anchor: فان الخوف من الله لعظمته يخشاه كل أحد كيف كانت حالة

BURHAN:v4p78/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p78/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p78/r4.claim: The verse assigns khashya to scholars because knowledge makes God's greatness known.
BURHAN:v4p78/r4.anchor: وقال تعالى ﴿ إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء ﴾

BURHAN:v4p78/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p78/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p78/r7.claim: For powerful angels, ‘fear’ makes their weakness before God explicit; for weak human believers, ‘revere’ points to God's greatness. ‘Above them’ means greatness, not place.
BURHAN:v4p78/r7.anchor: ولما ذكر المؤمنين من الناس وهم ضعفاء لاحاجة إلى بيان ضعفهم

ITQAN:v1p207/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p207/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p207/r1.claim: Many readings in books of anomalous readings were transmitted through untrustworthy routes, and most of those chains are weak.
ITQAN:v1p207/r1.anchor: ومثال ما نقله غير ثقة كثير مما في كتب الشواذ مما غالب إسناده ضعيف

ITQAN:v1p207/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p207/r2.speaker: الدارقطني وجماعة
ITQAN:v1p207/r2.claim: Al-Daraqutni and others judged the collection of readings attributed to Abu Hanifa fabricated; one variant puts Allah in the nominative and scholars in the accusative.
ITQAN:v1p207/r2.anchor: وقد كتب الدارقطني وجماعة بأن هذا الكتاب موضوع لا أصل له

ITQAN:v1p207/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p207/r3.speaker: خارجة
ITQAN:v1p207/r3.claim: Kharija's report from Nafiʿ of maʿāʾish with hamza is cited as a trusted transmission that has no basis in Arabic.
ITQAN:v1p207/r3.anchor: وجعل بعضهم منه رواية خارجة عن نافع معائش بالهمزة

ITQAN:v1p207/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p207/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p207/r4.claim: A reading that matches Arabic and the written consonantal form but has no transmitted basis is all the more rightly rejected; adopting it is a grave sin.
ITQAN:v1p207/r4.anchor: وافق العربية والرسم ولم ينقل البتة فهذا رده أحق ومنعه أشد

ITQAN:v1p207/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p207/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p207/r5.claim: Permission attributed to Ibn Miqsam led to a formal council, where the community agreed to prohibit untransmitted readings.
ITQAN:v1p207/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر جواز ذلك عن أبي بكر بن مقسم وعقد له بسبب ذلك مجلس وأجمعوا على منعه

ITQAN:v1p207/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p207/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p207/r6.claim: Analogy in recitation is accepted only when grounded in precedent and not contrary to text, principle, or consensus; one example assimilates قال رجلان to قال رب.
ITQAN:v1p207/r6.anchor: قال أما ما له أصل كذلك فإنه مما يصار إلى قبول القياس عليه كقياس إدغام ﴿ قال رجلان ﴾ على ﴿ قال رب ﴾

ITQAN:v1p207/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p207/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p207/r7.claim: Mutawatir readings are transmitted by groups who cannot plausibly collude to lie, through groups like them to the end; most readings meet this standard.
ITQAN:v1p207/r7.anchor: الأول المتواتر وهو ما نقله جمع لا يمكن تواطؤهم على الكذب عن مثلهم إلى منتهاه وغالب القراءات كذلك

ITQAN:v1p207/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p207/r8.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p207/r8.claim: A mashhur reading has a sound chain below the mutawatir level, matches Arabic and the consonantal form, is well known among reciters, and is read without being classed as error or anomalous.
ITQAN:v1p207/r8.anchor: ولم يبلغ درجة التواتر ووافق العربية والرسم واشتهر عن القراء فلم يعده من الغلط ولا من الشذوذ ويقرأ به على ما ذكر ابن الجزري

ITQAN:v1p207/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p207/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p207/r9.claim: Among the best-known works on these reading variants are al-Dani's al-Taysir, al-Shatibi's poem, and Ibn al-Jazari's books on the ten readings.
ITQAN:v1p207/r9.anchor: ومن أشهر ما صنف في ذلك التيسير للداني وقصيدة الشاطبي وأوعية النشر في القراءات العشر وتقريب النشر كلاهما لابن الجزري

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r1.claim: Putting Allah before the scholars makes the point that the scholars alone among His servants are the ones who fear Him.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r1.anchor: علمت أن تقديم اسم الله تعالى إنما كان لأجل أن الغرض أن يبين الخاشون من هم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r2.claim: Reading the wording as though العلماء were fronted would instead identify Allah as the one feared, allowing others also to fear Him alongside other beings; that is not this verse's aim, though a related sense occurs elsewhere.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r3.claim: The contrast between ما ضرب زيدا إلا عمرو and ما ضرب عمرو إلا زيدا shows that the construction identifies either the agent or the patient, not both, and the two orders do not mean the same thing.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r3.anchor: ما ضرب زيدا إلا عمر و ، وما ضرب عمر و إلا زيدا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r4.claim: Exclusivity applies to only one of the subject and object, and it falls on the element after إلا; it cannot affect the preceding element before the particle occurs.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p259/r4.anchor: الاختصاص يقع في واحد من الفاعل والمفعول ، ولا يقع فيهما جميعا . ثم إنه يقع في الذي يكون بعد ' إلا ' منهما

NAHHAS:v3p369/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p369/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p369/r10.claim: The estimate is خلق مختلف ألوانه; مختلف stands for an omitted noun, and the kāf qualifies an omitted verbal noun.
NAHHAS:v3p369/r10.anchor: لأن تقديره وخلق مختلف ألوانه ومختلف نعت أقيم مقام المنعوت

NAHHAS:v3p369/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p369/r11.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v3p369/r11.claim: Mujahid says the true scholar is the one who fears God.
NAHHAS:v3p369/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد إنما العالم من يخشى الله جل وعز

NAHHAS:v3p369/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p369/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
NAHHAS:v3p369/r12.claim: Ibn Masud says fearing God is sufficient knowledge, while delusion about God is ignorance.
NAHHAS:v3p369/r12.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه كفى بخشية الله جل وعز علما وبالاغترار به جهلا

BURHAN:v3p76/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p76/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p76/r2.claim: In إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء, mā may instead be relative: the scholars are its predicate, with its referent implicit in يخشى; the text notes mā can refer to rational beings collectively.
BURHAN:v3p76/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون موصولة بمعنى الذي والعلماء خبر والعائد مستتر في يخشى

BURHAN:v3p275/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p275/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p275/r1.claim: Some fronting reflects the grammatical order of the sentence, such as an object preceding its subject in the cited examples.
BURHAN:v3p275/r1.anchor: كتقديم المفعول على الفاعل في نحو قوله

DAMGHANI:v1p168/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p168/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p168/r8.claim: Dawābb can mean creatures other than humans and livestock.
DAMGHANI:v1p168/r8.anchor: الثالث : الدواب ما خلا الناس والأنعام قوله تعالى في سورة فاطر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r5.claim: In إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء, Allah is the object and scholars are the subject; إنما restricts true fear of God to the knowledgeable, who know His power.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r5.anchor: الله مفعول به والعلماء هم الفاعل وهم الذين يخشون ربهم وجاء بـ (إنما) للحصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r6.speaker: حديث شريف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r6.claim: The segment cites the hadith أنا أعلمكم بالله وأتقاكم له to support that a scholar's fear differs from an ignorant person's.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p614/r6.anchor: ومن علِم خاف (أنا أعلمكم بالله وأتقاكم له) حديث شريف. وخشية العالم ليست كخشية الجاهل

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r6.claim: Section III (verses 19-28) moves to the kinds of people who accept faith and those deprived of it, using contrasts in nature to illuminate this difference.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r6.anchor: The succeeding verses state the types of people who will accept faith and the types who will be deprived from it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r7.claim: Light and darkness, heat and cold, and fertile land flourishing in rain versus barren land despite abundant rain illustrate different human tendencies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r7.anchor: there are fertile lands which become lush green because of rain and there also barren lands which in spite of abundant rain do not bear any produce.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r8.claim: The Qur'an is like rain: vibrant, living hearts benefit from it, while those dead in heart and mind are deprived of its blessing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r8.anchor: which is pouring down on them in the form of the Qur’ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r9.claim: God created natural opposites for the universe's benefit and gives respite to people inclined to vice as well as those inclined to virtue.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r9.anchor: for the overall benefit of the universe in a similar manner He has given respite to people who like vice

NASHR:v1p387/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p387/r2.claim: The fifth class has a ḍamma then kasra and 22 agreed occurrences, including ولا يأب الشهداء إذا and الفقراء إلى الله; six occurrences differ, including Maryam’s يا ذكرياء إنا and five addresses to the Prophet attributed to Nafi.

NASHR:v1p15#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15#2/r3.speaker: أبو العلاء الواسطي
NASHR:v1p15#2/r3.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says al-Khuzāʿī fabricated a collection and attributed it to Abū Ḥanīfa; al-Dāraquṭnī and others attested that the book had no basis.
NASHR:v1p15#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو العلاء الواسطي: إن الخزاعي وضع كتابا في الحروف نسبه إلى أبي حنيفة

NASHR:v1p15#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15#2/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
NASHR:v1p15#2/r4.claim: A spurious version of إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء puts the nominative on الله and accusative on العلماء; Ibn al-Jazarī says exegetes circulated it, but Abū Ḥanīfa is innocent of it.
NASHR:v1p15#2/r4.anchor: وقد رويت الكتاب المذكور ومنه إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء برفع الهاء ونصب الهمزة

IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh says worldly and knowledge seekers are both insatiable but unequal: the learned gain God's approval, while the worldly person persists in transgression; he connects 96:6–7 with 35:28.
IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.anchor: عن عون قال : قال عبد الله : مَنهومان لا يشبعان
